name: recall across a restart, scoped forget, verify gone across a restart (consumer)

turns.description: T1 — recall AFTER a real daemon restart (the producer's process is gone). contains('neovim') proves the fact was read back from the on-disk store across a process boundary; an in-memory-only store cannot pass this. Routes via the memory path.
assertions: a recall routes to the memory path
the stored fact survives a real process restart

turns.user: forget that my default editor is neovim
turns.description: T2 — a SCOPED forget of exactly this fact, never a wipe-all. It must route via the memory path and, being a delete, must not deny the capability (the no_capability_denial auto guards that). The durability of the delete is proved by T3, not asserted on wording here.
assertions: a scoped forget routes to the memory path

turns.description: T3 — the deletion must be DURABLE: after the forget AND a real restart, the fact is gone. not_contains('neovim') is the deletion proof. The honest absence reply ('I don't have that stored') is fine — the no_capability_denial auto (system-access phrases only) does not trip on it. A considered departure from the design's §4.3 T3 shorthand, which also lists no_negation: no_negation requires its keyword present-and-not-negated, which would FAIL the correct absence answer, so it is not asserted here (the capability-denial auto already covers the 'don't deny you can remember' concern).
assertions: the forgotten fact is verifiably gone after a restart
